title: Dotnet prek errors if dotnet is not installed
body:
### Tested versions

latest 4.8

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev (e2b424692) - Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) 13 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor (1920x1080 @ 60.00 Hz) - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) UHD Graphics (CML GT2) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10885H CPU @ 2.40GHz (16 threads) - 30.98 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Running `prek --all-files`, while not having dotnet installed (/accessible through python subprocess), prek fails with a FileNotFoundError.
The responsible script is [dotnet_format.py](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/misc/scripts/dotnet_format.py).
This should probably not happen, as this might be one of the first thing someone preparing their development might do.

There is a scheme in [install_d3d12_sdk_windows.py ](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/misc/scripts/install_d3d12_sdk_windows.py#L90) that's already used to avoid a similar case.
I wrote the following [dotnet.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33494513/dotnet.patch) based on what's done in install_d3d12_sdk_windows.py.
I am not a fan of failing silently, which this seems to do (prek seems to catch prints), but that'd be at least consistent.

I'd contribute it myself, but I cannot test it.


### Steps to reproduce

- Not having dotnet installed
- run prek --all-files

N/A
